hints: Consider the circuit role required for signal current to return to the source.
Consider the shielding role of the outer conductor against external electromagnetic interference.
walkthrough: State that the copper braid provides the return path for the signal current (or completes the circuit / connects to ground).
State that the copper braid shields / screens the inner signal wire from external electromagnetic noise / interference.

ai_rubric.observable: States provides return for the signal (or completes circuit / ground return).
States shields signal from noise (or screens against external interference / radiation).

hints: Think of common everyday devices or laboratory setups that transmit high-frequency electrical signals with shielding.
Give an example such as connecting an aerial/antenna to a television set, or connecting signal generators/sensors to an oscilloscope.
walkthrough: State a practical application of coaxial cables in electrical signal transmission.
For example: connection between an aerial/antenna and a TV set (or connecting instruments to an oscilloscope / cable TV networks).

ai_rubric.observable: Suggests a valid application (e.g. connection between aerial and TV set, oscilloscope probe connection, cable television, LAN).

hints: Recall the formula for power ratio in decibels: ratio / dB = 10 lg(P_signal / P_noise).
Substitute SNR = 32 dB and P_noise = 7.6 × 10^-6 W, then solve for P_MIN.
walkthrough: Use the decibel SNR formula: 10 lg(P_MIN / P_noise) = 32 dB.

ai_rubric.observable: Recalls or uses decibel formula: gain / ratio in dB = 10 lg(P1 / P2) with substitution 32 = 10 lg[P_MIN / (7.6 × 10^-6)].
Calculates minimum signal power P_MIN = 0.012 W.

hints: Recall the relation for cable attenuation per unit length: attenuation per unit length = (1 / L) × 10 lg(P_in / P_out).
Substitute P_in = 2.6 W, P_out = 0.012 W, and attenuation rate = 6.3 dB km^-1, then solve for length L in km.
walkthrough: Use the attenuation equation: attenuation per unit length = (1 / L) × 10 lg(P_in / P_MIN).

ai_rubric.observable: Uses attenuation per unit length = (1 / L) × 10 lg(P1 / P2) with substitution 6.3 = (1 / L) × 10 lg(2.6 / 0.012).
Calculates maximum cable length L = 3.7 km.
